findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket, so objects (including the seeded vendor roster) are stored without enforced SSE-KMS/SSE-S3 encryption.
The bucket declares no ACL and has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block or bucket policy restricting public access, leaving it vulnerable to accidental public ACL/policy grants.
No logging block is configured, so object access to this data bucket is not recorded, hindering detection and forensic investigation of unauthorised access.
Versioning is disabled and force_destroy is true, so objects can be permanently overwritten or deleted (including by an attacker or a terraform destroy) with no recovery path.
The ledger export bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, so sensitive financial exports are stored unencrypted by default.
No logging block is configured for this bucket, so access to ledger data is not auditable.
Versioning is not enabled while force_destroy is true, allowing irreversible deletion or tampering of ledger export objects.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource guards this bucket; the private ACL alone does not prevent a later policy or ACL change from exposing it publicly.
Model artifact bucket defines versioning and logging but no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving stored artifacts unencrypted at rest.
No public access block is associated with this bucket, so public ACLs or bucket policies could be applied without being blocked at the account/bucket level.
The runbooks bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration; operational runbooks frequently contain sensitive procedural and connection detail and are stored unencrypted.
No logging block is configured, so reads and writes to the runbooks bucket are not recorded for audit.
The bucket lacks an aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block, relying solely on the private ACL to prevent public exposure.

The ACL value 'lcatalogopts-delivery-write' is not a valid canned S3 ACL (likely a corruption of 'log-delivery-write'), so the intended access control on the audit log bucket is not what is expressed; a malformed or mis-set ACL on the audit trail bucket risks either failed delivery or an unintended grant.

The bucket holding audit logs has no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block and grants write via a log-delivery style ACL; without a public access block, audit evidence could be exposed by a later ACL/policy change.
force_destroy = true on the audit/log bucket allows all audit evidence to be deleted non-interactively, and no object lock or MFA delete is configured to protect log integrity.

A vendor roster spreadsheet (likely containing third-party PII/business data) is uploaded with no server_side_encryption or kms_key_id argument into a bucket that also lacks default encryption, so it is stored in cleartext.
